name: Josip Broz Tito
description: Yugoslav leader assessed during his mature system of one-party government, federalism and worker self-management.

axes.brief: He retained one-party leadership and became president for life; participation occurred within socialist institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Worker participation and collective federal institutions qualify personal command but do not establish free national party competition.

qualifications.12: Internal institutional removal and entrenched lifelong leadership give opposing considerations.

axes.brief: Security police and repression of political challenges limited civil freedom, despite later easing of some controls.
axes.counterEvidence: Relative openness, travel and consumer culture compared with other socialist states qualify blanket censorship of all entertainment.

axes.brief: He promoted brotherhood and unity with recognised nationalities and languages in a multinational federation.
axes.counterEvidence: Repression of nationalist movements and insistence on Yugoslav unity qualify allowing distinct identities to trump the shared state.

qualifications.3: Shared Yugoslav participation and retained national customs coexist.
qualifications.9: Federal common purposes and multiple recognised traditions compete.

axes.brief: Non-aligned international exchange and labour mobility suggest regulated openness rather than ethnic migrant exclusion.
axes.counterEvidence: Domestic immigration is less explicit than emigration and diplomacy; modern visa mechanisms are contextual analogies.

qualifications.7: Labour mobility and economic capacity both matter.
qualifications.11: Administrative permission need not imply compulsory employer sponsorship.

axes.brief: He maintained substantial armed deterrence and citizen defence while mediating disputes and supporting negotiated disarmament.
axes.counterEvidence: Liberation-war experience and anti-colonial solidarity qualify a strict ban on all non-defensive military action.

axes.brief: Sovereign independence and non-alignment coexist with active UN engagement and international economic cooperation.
axes.counterEvidence: Cooperation and universal safeguards do not entail domination by either superpower or an external political federation.

qualifications.10: Human-rights diplomacy and one-party domestic sovereignty conflict under externally required law changes.

axes.brief: He favoured social ownership and worker-controlled enterprises rather than ordinary private capitalist ownership.
axes.counterEvidence: The bank’s binary public/private questions cannot directly express social ownership; public is used as the closer collective category, not a claim that all enterprises were state-administered. Small private farms and businesses remained.

axes.brief: International market participation and foreign joint ventures developed alongside protection of Yugoslav economic independence.
axes.counterEvidence: Quasi-market trade openness remained regulated and did not give foreign investors unlimited control over socially owned strategic firms.

qualifications.11: Retaliation and maintaining diverse trading relationships provide competing considerations.

axes.brief: Enterprises had meaningful production and wage discretion under broader social planning and investment priorities.
axes.counterEvidence: This is neither complete ministerial production command nor laissez-faire; worker ownership is assessed separately from price and production coordination.

axes.brief: Social rights, public services and equalising regional development were major purposes of the socialist federation.
axes.counterEvidence: Self-management produced earnings differences and regional inequality; compensation mechanisms are modern analogies where no exact position is documented.

axes.brief: Civil socialist institutions governed independently of clerical authority and religious teaching.
axes.counterEvidence: Later accommodation with religious communities and Catholic diplomatic ties qualify assuming all private worship was prohibited.

axes.brief: Women’s public participation and reproductive reform accompanied modernising socialist institutions and some retained family conventions.
axes.counterEvidence: Contemporary same-sex marriage and identity curricula were outside the explicit programme; estimates should not conflate socialist modernisation with every present-day reform.

qualifications.11: Social equality and conventional historical terminology give conflicting indications.
qualifications.15: Education and equality are plausible but specific modern curricula are undocumented.
qualifications.16: Inherited national cultures and socialist reform give competing reasons.

axes.brief: Industrialisation, infrastructure and nuclear energy show substantial technological ambition with negotiated safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Modern enhancement technologies are analogies; access to nuclear technology did not imply rejection of all safety controls.

axes.brief: He decentralised economic and constitutional responsibilities to republics while enforcing unity and repressing separatist challenges.
axes.counterEvidence: The 1974 settlement significantly expanded republic autonomy; personal leadership and party control must not erase that change.

axes.brief: Anti-racial international solidarity and socialist education support a social account of cooperative habits and opportunity.
axes.counterEvidence: His political programme does not quantify each temperament or attention mechanism; recognition of national cultures is not an inherited-race theory.
